lines: I still believe you can choose better. Let the first choice be removing that banner.
We can speak warmly again when you are no longer wearing a raider's threat.
Your deeds earned respect. Do not let that mark speak louder than all of them.
Leave the banner outside if you return.
Come back as the person this village respects.
Your good name deserves a better ending than that mark.
Take it down before the guards lose their patience.
I expect to see your own colors next time.
Do one more good thing today and put it away.
People still believe your better deeds show who you are. Do not prove them wrong.
The village would rather welcome its defender than fear a raider's symbol.
You have earned room to correct this, but not forever.
Let your next visit remind us why your name once brought relief.
Carry our gratitude with you and leave the banner behind.
The guards are waiting because they know your history. Respect that mercy.
One piece of cloth should not undo years of courage. Remove it.
Return peacefully and we can speak as old friends again.
Choose the reputation you built over the threat you found.
The children know your good stories. Do not give them a worse one today.
Go now, and make sure the banner is gone before anyone sees you return.
Take it off before you return. I would rather remember the person I trusted.
Do not make your friends look at that mark again.
Trust can survive a terrible choice, but only if you stop making it.
Put the banner away before we speak again.
I will wait for the friend I know, not the threat I see.
Do not ask our trust to survive another visit like this.
Lower it before someone less patient meets you outside.
Return without the raider mark and I will listen.
Give me a reason to defend your name after you leave.
I am letting you walk away because our history still means something.
Do not make me regret asking the guards to wait.
The next time I see you, I want to recognize the person first.
Friends can make terrible choices. They can also correct them.
Leave that mark on the road and come back with an explanation.
You know this village well enough to understand our fear.
Our trust is hurt, not gone. What you do next decides the rest.
Take the warning off your head before it reaches another door.
I will remember that you left peacefully if you choose to do so.
Do not carry a raider's threat into a place where you were welcomed.
Go carefully. People are frightened, and not everyone trusts you as I do.
Keep your distance until that banner is gone.
We are finished. Take the raider mark with you.
Your next greeting will go better without a threat above your face.
Remove the banner before you come back.
Our next conversation starts only after that mark is gone.
Keep away from the homes until you look peaceful again.
The guards will be watching the road behind you.
Leave without trouble and do not return dressed for a raid.
Make your choice before you reach another village gate.
We owe you no further hearing while you carry that sign.
Walk straight out and keep both hands visible.
If you meant no harm, leaving quietly is how you prove it.
Do not stop near the stores on your way to the gate.
The banner has made this meeting shorter than it could have been.
Set it down outside the walls if you expect to return.
You may explain yourself another day under a peaceful sky.
Nobody here knows you well enough to risk overlooking this.
The guards will not offer the same warning twice.
Take the open path and give every house a wide berth.
Go now. The village needs calm more than it needs your answer.
You have done nothing to ease my suspicion. That banner made it worse.
Leave now. I will be watching which way that mark travels.
We are done. Do not mistake restraint for trust.
Take the banner with you and stay away from our stores.
I will have more questions if you return.
Do not circle back after dark wearing that mark.
The guards know which road you took.
Lower it now, though that will not restore my trust.
Your next visit had better look very different from this one.
I will be checking whether anything is missing after you leave.
You arrived looking like my worst guess about you.
Do not test how closely the watch is following your steps.
If the banner is stolen, surrender it. If it is yours, leave with it.
Nothing about this encounter has made your purpose clearer.
Stay in sight until you are beyond the last house.
I expect the guards to search the path after you go.
Taking the mark down is only the first answer you owe us.
You have turned caution into a reason for alarm.
Do not approach another villager until you are rid of it.
Leave while this is still suspicion and not a fight.
Take your banner and get out of my sight.
No more words. That mark has said enough for you.
We are finished. Leave before this becomes something other than a conversation.
Get the banner and yourself out of here.
Come back under that mark and the guards will answer first.
Do not stop at another door on your way out.
I want you beyond sight of the bell before nightfall.
Take one peaceful step after another until this village is behind you.
There is nothing more to discuss. Leave.
You have worn out every warning this village owed you.
Take the quickest road away and do not turn back.
The banner suits the enemy you chose to become.
Nobody here will protect you from the guards now.
Keep away from our crops, our animals, and our homes.
I will sound the alarm myself if I see you again.
Your excuses can follow you out. We do not want them either.
One more threat and you will not leave under your own power.
This village has buried enough because of marks like that.
Go carry your hatred somewhere empty.
The conversation is over, and so is your welcome.
<shake>Please go.</shake> I cannot breathe easily while you wear that.
That is all I can say. Please take the banner away from here.
I answered you. Now let me get somewhere safe.
Please take that banner far from our homes.
Do not return until the raider mark is gone.
Stay on the open path where the guards can see you.
Please leave before fear turns into a fight.
Lower it before another villager mistakes your movement for an attack.
Go quietly and let the village settle again.
I have answered you. Please do not make me stay any longer.
Keep walking away and nobody needs to get hurt.
The children are watching from the windows. Please leave them in peace.
I will not follow you, so there is no need to threaten me.
Put it down before the guards decide you are reaching for a weapon.
Please use the wide path and avoid every doorway.
I want to believe you will leave without making the bell ring.
Do not come back tonight, even if you remove it.
My hands will stop shaking once you are beyond the wall.
Go now while everyone is still giving you room.
Please let this be the last time we see that mark.
